title: Thomas's early influences: Ory, Joe Oliver and Jack Carey
summary: Thomas recalls hearing Ory's band, Joe Oliver and Jack Carey in the country, and that he copied nobody.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I don't mean to cut you off, but when you were a kid like that, was there anybody you listened to that was your favorite, that you might copy out of?

Well, I used to listen, I used to listen at, see, Ori, Ori, Ori band originated out there in the country, in the Platt. Mm-hmm. After they came, they came down here and lived down here, well, they used to come out there and play, you know. Mm-hmm. Ori. And, uh.

Chip, yeah, Chip. I knew Chip, too. And, uh, it's because you come out there. I don't know what you call it. What he played? I don't know what you mean. Joe Oliver. He used to come out and play with Ori bands, you see. Uh-huh. And, uh, so, so, Jack Carey, Mud Carey, he used to come out and play, too. Mm-hmm. He came out and played with this band they had in the country. The older band was there before Washington. But after the trumpet player got drowned, well, they got him to play trumpet with them.

No. Yeah, yeah. Uh-huh. Yeah. So, well, it got him to play trumpet. Mm-hmm. So, but I liked it. I liked the Joe Oliver playing, you know what I mean? But I never did cop at nobody, you see. Oh, I see. I never did, you know, no patron at nobody. I played my own, my own way. We all, we all played our own way. Yeah.
